description: S459 copy-in (N2): `@rows = r` stores a copy of the local array `r`. Writing through `r` afterwards (`r[0].n = -5`, `r.push({ …, n: -5 })` — writes the unrefined local admits) changes `r` only: @rows keeps [{ u: "o", n: 4 }] and nothing is refused. Before copy-in @rows held `r` itself, and both writes landed in `L[]` unjudged.
rationale: §53.3.3: the assignment is applied only if the predicate holds, and the variable otherwise retains its prior value — a write through another reference must not be able to change a refined cell without its check. ruling:user-voice-scrml.md S459 "a, go" (copy on the way in); analogy:§66.10.
